extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent attorneys and IP practitioners interested in expedited/exam-priority procedures at the Brazilian Patent and Trademark Office (INPI)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on routes, eligibility and procedural requirements for requesting priority/expedited examination of patent applications at Brazil's INPI, including use of the Patent Prosecution Highway (PPH).

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant-related prioritisation eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: The examination can be prioritised in situations related to the applicant, as follows: individual applicants who are over 60 years of age, when the applicant has physical or mental disabilities, or suffer from a severe illness, or even when the applicant is a micro or small company, a Scientific, Technological and Innovation Institution or a start-up.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These applicant-based categories are explicitly listed as grounds for requesting prioritised examination; use of these grounds has contributed positively to reducing time to examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject-matter prioritisation
rubrics_metrics.description: The prioritisation of applications can also be requested due to their subject matter, including the matter involve green technology, treatments for specific diseases such as AIDS, cancer, and rare diseases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subject-matter categories (environmental/health-critical technologies) are eligible for priority requests and are treated as distinct grounds alongside applicant-related reasons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Circumstantial reasons for prioritisation
rubrics_metrics.description: There are circumstantial reasons that also allow examination to be prioritised, namely, in cases of patent applications related to technology available on the Brazilian market or when there is a threat of unauthorised use by third parties of the technology that is the subject matter of the patent application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the technology is already on the market in Brazil or there is risk of unauthorised use, this can justify an expedited examination request under INPI practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Prosecution Highway (PPH) entry condition
rubrics_metrics.description: The Patent Prosecution Highway (PPH) is ... where, after a partner patent office deems the subject matter of a patent application patentable, it becomes possible to prioritise examination of the patent application for the same invention at the INPI.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PPH is one of the primary mechanisms to expedite examination; INPI data (2021–22) show substantial uptake and that it is an efficient route to speed prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence waiver under Ordinance INPI/PR Nº 78/22 (PPH)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ordinance INPI/PR Nº 78/22 ... afforded another benefit to applicants, the waiver of the need to submit the approval of the corresponding patent application provided that the Examiner of the Partner Patent Office is of the opinion that there is patentable subject matter in the claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In practice any document indicating existence of patentable subject matter may be used (e.g., a European Search Opinion stating that the claims meet the requirements of novelty, inventive step and industrial application). This relaxes the former requirement to submit formal approval from the partner office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual limit of PPH requests per IPC
rubrics_metrics.description: The total limit of requests per International Patent Classification (IPC) per year has been increased from 150 to 250.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a quantitative, per-IPC cap that affects availability of PPH entry for certain technical fields—applicants should consider IPC demand when planning PPH requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible Partner Patent Offices for INPI PPH
rubrics_metrics.description: The INPI has a partnership with the following Partner Patent Offices: USA, China, Europe, Japan, United Kingdom, South Korea, France, Austria, Denmark, Sweden, Singapore, Portugal, Spain and PROSUL (Argentina, Chile, Colombia, Costa Rica, Dominican Republic, El Salvador, Ecuador, Nicaragua, Panama, Paraguay, Peru and Uruguay).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PPH requests at INPI rely on these partner offices; positive findings from examiners at these offices can be the basis for accelerated processing at INPI.

rubrics_metrics.name: PPH performance and acceptance metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: In 2021 and 2022, the INPI received around 1290 requests for entrance into the PPH programme and the average time between the submission of the PPH request and the publication of a first technical opinion was about 4 months. In addition, the average time between the submission of PPH request and the issuance of a final decision (approval or rejection) was about 6 months. It should be noted that in the last two years, 96% of requests for entrance in the programme were accepted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These empirical metrics indicate the practical efficiency and high acceptance rate of PPH at INPI; applicants can use these timelines when choosing expedited routes.
